chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from an-Nadr from 'Abdullah ibn Sinan from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about staying with the people of the kharam (tax-paying locals), and he said, 'Three days.' This was narrated from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family).
ai.seo_question: What is the prescribed duration of stay for travelers in tax-paying regions according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the customary duration for officials or travelers to reside in *Ahl al-Kharaj* (land tax-paying) regions, establishing a three-day limit rooted in Prophetic tradition. It reflects the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on administrative fairness and the integration of pre-Islamic Arab customs (*urf*) into Islamic law, ensuring that temporary stays do not become burdensome or permanent impositions on the local populace.
